extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: TravelPlanner is a benchmark crafted for evaluating language agents in tool-use and complex planning within multiple constraints, grounded in travel planning scenarios. It provides a rich sandbox environment with around four million data entries accessible via six tools, and 1,225 meticulously curated planning intents with reference plans. The benchmark evaluates whether agents can develop flexible travel plans by collecting information via diverse tools and making decisions while satisfying environment constraints, commonsense constraints, and hard constraints (user needs).
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su
extraction.publisher: Fudan University, The Ohio State University, The Pennsylvania State University, Meta AI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was constructed through the following steps: (1) Environment and evaluation setup with a static sandbox containing around four million data entries crawled from the Internet accessible via six tools; (2) Diverse travel query design based on fundamental elements like departure city, destination, and date range, with varying duration (3, 5, or 7 days) and difficulty levels (easy, medium, hard); (3) Reference plan annotation by 20 graduate students; (4) Quality check by authors.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Flight data from Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset (spanning 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01); Distance data from Google Distance Matrix API; Restaurant data from Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset; Attraction data from Google Places API; Accommodation data from Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data was modified from public sources including adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to avoid data contamination. For flights, 'Price' was generated by multiplying 'Distance' by a random factor ranging from 0.2 to 0.5. For distance matrix, 'Price' for self-driving and taxi modes was calculated by multiplying 'Distance' by factors of 1 and 0.15. Restaurants were randomly assigned to cities and categorized under cuisines. Accommodations were randomly assigned cities and random room rules.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: From flight dataset, fields like 'FlightDate', 'DepTime', 'ArrTime', 'ActualElapsedTime', 'Distance', 'OriginCityName', 'DestCityName' were extracted. From restaurant dataset, 'Restaurant Name' and 'Average Cost' were extracted. From accommodations, 'NAME', 'room type', 'price', 'minimum nights', 'review rate number', 'maximum occupancy' were extracted. Queries were re-calibrated using costs from corresponding human-annotated plans.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 20 graduate students were invited to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries. A plan is deemed eligible only if it meets all constraints outlined in the evaluation script. This process resulted in 1,225 validated query-plan pairs. Authors performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Authors re-calibrated each query's budget using the costs from corresponding human-annotated plans, replacing initial heuristic-generated budgets. Multiple stages of human verification were conducted to ensure high quality and the presence of at least one feasible solution.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 reference plan per query (1,225 validated query-plan pairs)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 graduate students. Annotators were paid an average of $0.80 for each plan annotated. Annotators averagely took 12 minutes to manually annotate a plan.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used to generate natural language queries); GPT-4-Turbo (used for key components extraction from plans)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: TravelPlanner aims to provide an effective benchmark for complex planning in future research, potentially helping to automate tedious planning tasks. The authors envision it as a catalyst for future research in enhancing agents' performance in increasingly complex scenarios, contributing to the broader quest for AI abilities.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The definition of commonsense may vary; current evaluation criteria are based on the authors' consensus, and the authors encourage additional discussions to enrich the commonsense dimension.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Some data in the TravelPlanner environment is derived from publicly available data on the Internet, and the content involved does not represent the authors' viewpoints. Current agents struggle with this benchmark: GPT-4 only achieves 0.6% final pass rate. The commonsense criteria are based on authors' consensus and may not be exhaustive.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training set (45 pairs, 5 queries per group) for learning with feedback such as reinforcement learning; Validation set (180 queries, 20 per group) and Test set (1,000 queries) for evaluation. Cheating in validation and test sets is strictly prohibited to uphold fairness. The benchmark evaluates language agents' tool-use and planning capabilities in multi-constraint scenarios. Two modes: two-stage (tool-use + planning) and sole-planning mode.
